record.paper_title: Constructing groups of 'small' order: Recent results and open problems
record.original_question: Let L_n denote the isomorphism types of finite groups of order n. For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 20000 such that 2^10 divides n or 3^9 divides n, can L_n be completely enumerated, including both nilpotent and non-nilpotent groups? These are the orders in the source's case E1, where the obstruction is the very large number of p-groups already present at orders 2^10 and 3^9.

artifact.self_contained_problem: For a positive integer $n$, let $L_n$ denote the set of isomorphism types of finite groups of order $n$. Determine $L_n$ explicitly (i.e., produce a complete, irredundant list of all isomorphism types of finite groups of order $n$, including both nilpotent and non-nilpotent groups) for every integer $n$ with $1 \le n \le 20000$ such that $2^{10} \mid n$ or $3^9 \mid n$. The principal obstruction is that the number of $p$-groups of order $2^{10}$ and of order $3^9$ is already extremely large (for instance, there are $49{,}487{,}365{,}422$ groups of order $1024$), so the question is whether a complete enumeration can nonetheless be carried out for all such $n$ in the stated range.
artifact.status_search_result: The GAP SmallGroups library (current version 1.5.4, 2024) still excludes order 1024 due to the roughly 4.95×10^10 groups of that order, and orders divisible by 1024 or by 3^9 within 1–20000 remain not fully enumerated in standard libraries. No complete enumeration of all groups of these orders (including non-nilpotent ones) is reported in the literature, so the problem appears to be open.

status_evidence.title: SmallGrp - The GAP Small Groups Library 1.5.4
status_evidence.snippet: The library contains groups of order at most 2000 except 1024.
status_evidence.claim: Order 1024 is excluded from the SmallGroups library, so groups of orders divisible by 1024 are not fully enumerated there.

status_evidence.title: On the number of groups of order 1024
status_evidence.claim: The enormous count of 2-groups of order 1024 is the principal obstruction to completing the enumeration.

status_evidence.title: Constructing groups of 'small' order: recent results and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Case E1 lists orders n ≤ 20000 with 2^10 | n or 3^9 | n as open.
status_evidence.claim: Enumeration for these orders is listed as an open problem.
